speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have presented with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin our evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms? Additionally, have you noticed any recent neck pain or trauma to the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of diabetes, alcohol use, and steroid use alongside unexplained weight loss, I am concerned about potential neuropathy or a malignancy affecting your brachial plexus. REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, HbA1c, and Tumor Markers (CEA, CA-15-3, CA 19-9). Do you experience any night sweats, fever, or changes in bowel habits recently?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing right brachial plexus apical syndrome.

The combination of progressive right arm weakness, sensory loss, unexplained weight loss, and your history of heavy smoking and diabetes is highly suspicious for an apical lung tumor compressing the lower trunk of the brachial plexus. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CTA or Chest_MRI to visualize the lung apex and brachial plexus involvement.
